preamble.summary: Proverbs 21 concentrates on divine-sovereignty-over-human-hearts (v. 1) and sacrifice-vs-justice theology (vv. 3, 27). Verse 3 — 'to do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice' — joins the prophetic-ethical-critique-of-sacrifice family (1 Sam 15:22, Ps 40:6, Ps 51:16, Hos 6:6, Mic 6:6–8, Isa 1:11–17).
preamble.notable_variants: 21:1 'the king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD' divine-sovereignty over rulers; 21:3 'righteousness and justice more acceptable than sacrifice' — prophetic-ethical tradition; 21:9 'better to live in a corner of the housetop than with a quarrelsome wife.'

variant_notes: 'The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the LORD; he turns it wherever he will' tracks MT. KING'S-HEART-IN-GOD'S-HAND — divine-sovereignty even over rulers. Romans 13:1 ('the authorities have been instituted by God') extends.
'Every way of a man is right in his own eyes, but the LORD weighs the heart' tracks MT. // Prov 16:2.

'To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to the LORD than sacrifice' tracks MT. RIGHTEOUSNESS-OVER-SACRIFICE. Joins 1 Sam 15:22, Ps 40:6, 51:16, Hos 6:6, Mic 6:6–8 tradition. Jesus' 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' (Matt 9:13, 12:7, citing Hos 6:6) extends.
'Haughty eyes and a proud heart, the lamp of the wicked, are sin' tracks MT.
'The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty' tracks MT.
'The getting of treasures by a lying tongue is a fleeting vapor and a snare of death' tracks MT.
'The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to do what is just' tracks MT.
'The way of the guilty is crooked, but the conduct of the pure is upright' tracks MT.
'It is better to live in a corner of the housetop than in a house shared with a quarrelsome wife' tracks MT. // Prov 21:19, 25:24.
'The soul of the wicked desires evil; his neighbor finds no mercy in his eyes' tracks MT.
'When a scoffer is punished, the simple becomes wise; when a wise man is instructed, he gains knowledge' tracks MT.
'The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked; he throws the wicked down to ruin' tracks MT.
'Whoever closes his ear to the cry of the poor will himself call out and not be answered' tracks MT. Reciprocal-justice — failure-to-hear-the-poor brings unanswered-prayer.
'A gift in secret averts anger, and a concealed bribe, strong wrath' tracks MT.
'When justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers' tracks MT.
'One who wanders from the way of good sense will rest in the assembly of the dead' tracks MT.
'Whoever loves pleasure will be a poor man; he who loves wine and oil will not be rich' tracks MT.

'The wicked is a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous for the upright' tracks MT. RANSOM-SUBSTITUTION theology — the wicked pays-the-price for the righteous. Proto-substitutionary-atonement vocabulary.
'It is better to live in a desert land than with a quarrelsome and fretful woman' tracks MT. // v. 9 variant.
'Precious treasure and oil are in a wise man's dwelling, but a foolish man devours it' tracks MT.
'Whoever pursues righteousness and kindness will find life, righteousness, and honor' tracks MT.
'A wise man scales the city of the mighty and brings down the stronghold in which they trust' tracks MT.
'Whoever keeps his mouth and his tongue keeps himself out of trouble' tracks MT.
'Scoffer is the name of the arrogant, haughty man who acts with arrogant pride' tracks MT.
'The desire of the sluggard kills him, for his hands refuse to labor' tracks MT.
'All day long he craves and craves, but the righteous gives and does not hold back' tracks MT. GIVES-AND-DOES-NOT-HOLD-BACK — generosity-as-diagnostic.
'The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with evil intent' tracks MT.
'A false witness will perish, but the word of a man who hears will endure' tracks MT.
'A wicked man puts on a bold face, but the upright gives thought to his ways' tracks MT.

'No wisdom, no understanding, no counsel can avail against the LORD' tracks MT. NOTHING-AVAILS-AGAINST-THE-LORD. 1 Corinthians 1:19–20 ('where is the wise one? where is the scribe? … has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?') extends the divine-sovereignty-over-wisdom theology.
'The horse is made ready for the day of battle, but the victory belongs to the LORD' tracks MT. HORSE-PREPARED / VICTORY-BELONGS-TO-LORD. Ps 20:7, 33:17 echo the anti-military-confidence tradition.
